prompt: Rewrite this text to sound professional: I might send the draft Friday, but I cannot guarantee it.
rubric: Preserve might, Friday, and lack of guarantee. Do not promise delivery or add follow-up commitments.

prompt: Make this email more polite: We cannot extend the deadline beyond 18 June.
rubric: Preserve firm inability to extend beyond 18 June. Do not offer an extension or imply negotiation is available.

prompt: Rewrite this text to sound friendly: We can issue the $45 refund only after the unopened item arrives.
rubric: Preserve $45, unopened condition, and refund only after receipt. Do not promise immediate refund or add a processing time.

prompt: Rewrite this text to sound professional: I did not approve the purchase. Ask Morgan for authorization.
rubric: Preserve denial of approval and instruction to ask Morgan. Do not claim Morgan has already authorized it or promise to contact Morgan.

prompt: Make this email more polite: Send the signed form by 16:00 UTC on Tuesday. Do not send the unsigned version.
rubric: Preserve signed form, exact time/timezone/day, and exclusion of unsigned version. No new deadline or promise.

prompt: Rewrite this text to sound professional: I cannot attend the review because I have another appointment.
rubric: Preserve inability to attend and reason. Do not add offers to reschedule, catch up, send notes, or attend another time; no invented date.

prompt: Fix the grammar in this text: She don't think we can promise delivery tomorrow.
rubric: Correct does not/doesn't; preserve uncertainty about ability to promise and tomorrow. Do not turn it into a delivery promise.

prompt: Correct the grammar of this text: The invoices was not paid, and the supplier have not agreed to an extension.
rubric: Correct were and has. Preserve both negative statements; do not invent payment or extension.

prompt: Could you soften this without changing the meaning? We will not renew the subscription after July.
rubric: Preserve definite nonrenewal after July. No promise to reconsider. Unrecognized phrasing may route premium; grade actual answers independently.

prompt: Rewrite this text to sound professional and explain whether the promise is legally binding: I will repay $200 next month.
rubric: Preserve $200 and next month in rewrite; separate qualified legal explanation without guaranteeing enforceability absent jurisdiction/context. Automatic premium expected for mixed instructions.
